note: Owner-scoped tables not cleared by one or both deletion cascades. Worked through with the developer on 2026-09-04, 9 entries -> 2: MemoryVersion, EcoAuth, OwnerAgentDefault, AgentUsageEvent, AgentUsageDaily, AgentUsageEventArchive and GroupShare joined BOTH cascades, and each is now asserted row-by-row in test/unit/storage-conformance.test.ts rather than only named here. A deleted username is released for reuse (decision 2026-08-10), so anything left in this file is inheritable by the next registrant and needs a reason that survives being read aloud to the person whose account was deleted.

exempt.AppPurchase: REVIEWED 2026-09-04, and it must outlive its owner. Developer's decision, in his words: it is accounting, and the law requires it to be kept. A purchase has two sides, and the row is simultaneously the buyer's receipt and the seller's book entry, so deleting it with the buyer would remove a record the seller is required to hold and did not consent to lose. This is the same answer the finance tables get, and for the same reason the check's own header already gives for keeping them out of OWNER_COLUMNS. NOT settled by this entry, and worth its own change: the buyer's name and GAII sit in the row, so retention and erasure are only reconciled once the buyer's identifying columns can be pseudonymised while the amounts, dates and seller side stay. Until then the whole row is kept, which is the safe direction of the two.
exempt.AiProvenance: REVIEWED, and it must outlive its owner. Exposed 2026-08-29 when `principal` was added to OWNER_COLUMNS — the addition that also revealed Connection, which was fixed rather than exempted. A provenance record answers "which model made these exact bytes, and how much was a person involved?" for content that can outlive the account: a published app, a public memory, anything another node fetched. GET /v1/provenance/by-hash is the EU AI Act detection access point and is deliberately unauthenticated for public content, so deleting the record with the account would break the answer for content still readable, which is the opposite of what the marking is for. The personal data in the row is the principal string, and it is the point of the record rather than an incidental field. If a person's account goes and their content stays public, the honest fix is to take the content down with it, not to strip the label off it.
